title: On Man, in His Own Image Made
description: On Man, in His Own Image Made in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 8 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book I, hymn 1, “Adam. Gen 3:9”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: On man, in his own i-mage made, How much did God be-stow? The whole cre-a-tion hom-age paid, And owned him Lord, be-low!

lines: On man, in his own image made,
He dwelt in Eden's garden, stored
And there with his descending Lord
But O! by sin how quickly changed!
His heart, from God and truth, estranged,
Now from his Maker's voice he flees,
And thinks to hide, amidst the trees,
Compelled to answer to his name,
He cast, on God himself, the blame,
But grace, unasked, his heart subdued
By faith, the promised seed he viewed,
And felt his pow'r to save.
But when by faith the sinner sees
Then he forsakes his foolish pleas,

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
